Text:
Around East Texas, a side-by-side can be a fence-checker one day, a hunting-camp ride the next, and a way to spend time with family on the weekend.

That is why it helps not to assume the auto policy on your pickup automatically follows the ATV or UTV behind it. The machine, the trailer, where it is used, the people who ride in it, and added equipment can all be worth discussing before the next trip down a trail or across the pasture.

Our new guide walks through a few simple questions to bring to that conversation, from the year, make, model, and VIN to photos of a winch, roof, lights, or other accessories.

Read the plain-language guide in our Resources section: https://morrison-ins.net/resources/atv-utv-insurance-east-texas

Before the next ride, pull together the basics: the machine’s year, make, model, VIN, estimated value, where it is used, and a few photos of added equipment. It also helps to think about the trailer and the usual riders.

Text:
ATVs, UTVs, and side-by-sides are useful in many different ways around Shelby County. One may be used to check fences, carry supplies, work around a farm or ranch, head to a hunting lease, or enjoy a trail with family.

Those different uses are a good reason to take a few minutes to understand how the machine is listed and what information belongs in an insurance conversation. A current record of the year, make, model, VIN, estimated value, trailer, usual riders, and added equipment can make that review easier.
